findings.title: Contradictory statements about edits to upstream slices
findings.description:
The design does not say consistently which upstream modules this slice edits, so the task breakdown cannot be derived from it.
- Line 42 says "No edits to 424 or 425", but lines 321 and 426 widen 424's `CaseDrop.reason`, and line 87 / D17 change 425's `bench_report.py`.
- Line 451 allows `tests/benchmark/` to change "where D8 routes re-qualification and D17 extracts the interval". D8 says 424's `replay_one` already calls `runner.requalify`, and D17 says "No change to 425". Line 451 reads like text from an earlier revision.
- Line 424 adds `ScrubbedEnvironment.with_tools` to 421, and `yield_report.py` (422) gains rows, while D7 says "no 422 code changes".

Fix: replace line 42 with one explicit list of upstream touches (421 `with_tools`, 422 yield rows, 424 `CaseDrop.reason`, 425 `bench_report`, 177 extractions) and correct line 451 to match.

findings.title: Over-size record lifecycle can leave a case both judged and counted as over size
findings.description:
D14 says raising the limit and rerunning `judge` judges the case, and D15 says the `OverSizeCase` "is replaced when the limit changes". Its id (D16) excludes the limit, and nothing replaces it once the case is no longer over size.
- **Limit raised:** the stale `OverSizeCase` stays beside the new `DiffJudgment`s.
- **Limit lowered, or a resumed run adds a larger replay:** existing judgments stay beside a new `OverSizeCase`.

The report (D17) has no rule for which record wins, so the "over size N" count the slice plan requires can be wrong. Walkthrough step 7 avoids the problem by using a fresh benchmark id. Fix: state one rule, such as deleting the record when the case is judged, or having the report ignore an `OverSizeCase` whose `max_prompt_chars` differs from the current limit or whose case has judgments.

findings.title: Judging of incomplete cases is unspecified
findings.description:
D13 and D15 cover committed replays, config absences (forfeit) and harness absences (drop). They do not cover a (case, config, sample) with no replay record yet, which is the normal state after a run stopped at its cap.

The architecture says a partial run "reports only cases that completed under every config", and "absent is not zero" means a pending replay must not count as a forfeit. As written, `judge` could spend calls on a case the report then excludes as `incomplete` (425 D13), or record a pending side as a forfeit that resume never re-judges. Fix: state that a case is judged only when every config has all k samples recorded, and count the rest as pending in the bound and summary.

findings.title: Separate judge cap departs from the architecture without saying so
findings.description: The architecture's run-level cap "covers grading and judging as well as the replays". D16 gives `judge` its own `--max-cost`, following 425 D9. 425 records this as a departure and asks for the architecture's cost section to be updated; 426 should carry the same sentence for judging. The per-call figure is the largest observed cost, so "at most $3.88" is an estimate when prompts can reach 400k characters; 425 D9 says this about its own figure and D16 should too.

findings.title: Reference is the branch tip, not the landing commit
findings.description: The architecture and the slice plan both say "the landing commit is the reference". D2 uses `tip_sha` and gives the reason: on a merge landing, `fork..after` includes unrelated target work. This is a sound refinement, but the architecture wording should be updated to match.

findings.title: `cf` on the scrubbed PATH: the spike should cover cf's runtime
findings.description:
D9 links only the `cf` executable into `<id>.home/bin`. If cf starts through an interpreter resolved from `PATH`, that interpreter is not on the scrubbed `PATH` (421: adapter entries, `home/bin`, system dirs).
- The spike should check this explicitly, since the fix would widen `PATH` further against the principle that it "leaves out the user's tool installs".
- The design should say what happens when `cf` is missing from the harness `PATH`: refuse at planning, not a harness absence per replay.

The deviation from the principle is otherwise bounded: slice runner only, and not part of `EnvironmentIdentity`.

findings.title: Minor unspecified items
findings.description:
- `--keep` on `slice-cases build` is in the signature but not described. It presumably keeps sandboxes as in 422.
- In the report example, the `pairs` value `18+` is unexplained, and D17 does not say whether the per-config W/L/T columns include vs-reference pairs. The example's numbers imply cross-config pairs only.

findings.title: Alignment with architecture principles and slice-plan scope
findings.description:
- **Production pipeline:** replays run producer-only `P6` with no copied step or prompt.
- **Hidden and superseded sets:** the hidden set is empty, and a slice's own tests are ignored (the "no slice tests as hidden tests" non-goal). The superseded set comes from 422's closure digests.
- **Qualification:** mechanical, keyed on environment, with every rejection recorded under an enum reason.
- **Objective before opinion:** per-kind tables keep slice and fix cases apart, pairwise results sit beside the objective grade, and there is no composite.
- **Reference:** it is a contestant in the fit but shown as an unranked reference line.
- **Diff rules:** normalization matches the architecture's list (the `uv.lock` addition is flagged and justified), and the over-size rule is "excluded and counted", with no truncation.
- **Absences:** config absences forfeit and harness absences drop the case, matching "absent is not zero".
- **Store:** new records are optional sibling payloads with sidecar diffs.
- **Dependencies:** directions are correct, and the seams it uses (`CaseKindRunner.requalify`, `bootstrap_mean_interval`, 425's empty-hidden-set grading) are what 424 and 425 say they provide to 426.

findings.title: Failure modes and proportionality
findings.description:
- **Failure modes:** each new I/O path has a stated, observable outcome. Git calls give `harness_error` with an ERROR log. cf steps that fail or time out give a harness absence with stderr. Judge calls are bounded by `metrology.judge_timeout_s`, and a failed pair is left unrecorded, logged and retried. A missing `tip_sha` is a named refusal. The success criteria require a test per signal.
- **Proportionality:** the four layers map to the slice-plan entry. D13's pairing cuts judge calls by more than half against all-pairs, the bounded-view judge and landing splicing are deferred, and no new protocol or dependency is added. Nothing obvious to cut.
